content.text:
Landès Lewitin (November 14, 1892 – January 20, 1966) was an American painter and theorist who was a significant figure in the postwar New York School. Born in Cairo and trained in Paris, he was known for his work involving color, collage, and symbolism.

Lewitin was a founding figure of **The Club**, which was formed in 1949 by a group of artists, including Philip Pavia. He was the first name listed on the club's 1952 charter membership list and played a vital role in shaping its intellectual direction. The Club served as a central discussion forum for artists, critics, and curators, playing a key role in the development of Abstract Expressionism and postwar American modernism. Artist Jeanne Patterson Miles later described Lewitin and Pavia as "the backbone of the Club."
